questions.q: (a) How many digits can the product of a 6-digit and a 4-digit number have? (b) Write the smallest such product with Indian commas.
(a) How many digits can a 9-digit number times a 2-digit number have? (b) Can the product have 9 digits? Explain with the smallest product.
questions.a: (a) 10 or 11 digits. (b) No. The smallest product is 10,00,00,000 x 10 = 1,00,00,00,000 which has 10 digits, so 9 digits is impossible.
s: Part (b): shows the smallest product has 10 digits so 9 is impossible

questions.q: (a) Find the smallest and the largest product of two 2-digit numbers. (b) How many digits does each have?
questions.a: (a) 10 x 10 = 100 and 99 x 99 = 9,801. (b) 100 has 3 digits and 9,801 has 4 digits.

questions.q: (a) Without multiplying, how many digits can 456 x 789 have? (b) Use 400 x 700 to show it has 6 digits, and then check with the exact product 3,59,784.
questions.a: (a) 3-digit x 3-digit gives 5 or 6 digits. (b) 456 > 400 and 789 > 700, so the product exceeds 400 x 700 = 2,80,000, which has 6 digits; the exact product 3,59,784 has 6 digits.
s: Part (b): lower bound 2,80,000 gives 6 digits, matching 3,59,784

questions.q: Show that the product of a 3-digit number and a 3-digit number can never have 4 digits.
questions.a: The smallest 3-digit number is 100, so the smallest product is 100 x 100 = 10,000, which already has 5 digits. Every other product is at least that big, so it can never have 4 digits.
s: Concludes no product can have 4 digits

questions.q: A product has exactly 9 digits. Create two different shapes (m-digit x n-digit) that can give a 9-digit product and justify each with an example.
questions.a: Any shapes with m + n = 9 or 10 work. For example 5-digit x 5-digit: 10,000 x 10,000 = 10,00,00,000 (9 digits). 4-digit x 5-digit: 9,999 x 99,999 = 99,98,90,001 (9 digits).
s: Names two different valid shapes (m + n is 9 or 10)
Justifies the first with a 9-digit example
Justifies the second with a 9-digit example

questions.q: (a) State the smallest and largest product of two 3-digit numbers and the number of digits each has. (b) How many digits can a 6-digit x 3-digit product have? (c) Can 4,57,326 x 893 be a 9-digit number? Give the exact product to check.
questions.a: (a) Smallest 100 x 100 = 10,000 (5 digits); largest 999 x 999 = 9,98,001 (6 digits). (b) 8 or 9 digits. (c) Yes, it can: 4,57,326 x 893 = 40,83,92,118, which has 9 digits.
s: Part (c): says yes using the 8-or-9 range

questions.q: A cinema chain's software multiplies the ticket price (a 3-digit number) by the number of tickets sold in a year (a 6-digit number) and stores the result in a field of 8 digit boxes. (a) Find the smallest and the largest possible products for this shape. (b) How many digits can the result have? (c) Check with price 450 and 5,20,000 tickets: how many digits does 450 x 5,20,000 = 23,40,00,000 have? (d) Is the field of 8 boxes safe? What is the smallest safe length?
questions.a: (a) Smallest 100 x 1,00,000 = 1,00,00,000; largest 999 x 9,99,999 = 99,89,99,001. (b) 8 or 9 digits. (c) 23,40,00,000 has 9 digits. (d) No: 9-digit results are possible and occur. The smallest safe length is 9 boxes.
s: Part (d): says 8 boxes is unsafe and 9 boxes is the smallest safe length

questions.q: A housing society in Hyderabad has 240 flats. Assume each flat uses 500 litres of water a day. A water tanker brings 12,000 litres and the society has booked 6 tankers a day, which is 42 tankers a week. (a) How many litres does the whole society use in a day? (b) How many litres in a week of 7 days? (c) How many tanker loads are needed every day? (d) The secretary says the booking of 42 tankers a week is enough. Using (b) and (c), is she right? Say by how many litres a week the supply is off, and name the assumption your answer depends on.
questions.a: (a) 240 x 500 = 1,20,000 litres a day. (b) 1,20,000 x 7 = 8,40,000 litres a week. (c) 1,20,000 / 12,000 = 10 tankers a day (70 a week). (d) No. 42 tankers bring 42 x 12,000 = 5,04,000 litres, which is 8,40,000 - 5,04,000 = 3,36,000 litres short in a week (28 tankers short, 70 - 42). This depends on the assumption of 500 litres per flat per day.
s: Part (c): 1,20,000 / 12,000 = 10 tankers a day, so 70 a week
Part (d): says no, 5,04,000 supplied is 3,36,000 short of 8,40,000, and names the 500 litres assumption

questions.q: Rahul decides to run 8 km every day for 25 years. The Moon is 3,84,400 km from the Earth. Work in stages (take 365 days in a year). (a) How far does he run in one year? (b) How far in 25 years? (c) Can he reach the Moon this way? (d) How many days are there in 25 years, and what is the smallest whole number of km he must run each day to cover 3,84,400 km in that time?
questions.a: (a) 8 x 365 = 2,920 km. (b) 2,920 x 25 = 73,000 km. (c) No, 73,000 km is less than 3,84,400 km. (d) 365 x 25 = 9,125 days. 42 km a day gives 3,83,250 km, which falls short, and 43 km a day gives 3,92,375 km, so the smallest whole number is 43 km a day.
s: Part (c): compares with 3,84,400 and says he cannot reach
Part (d): tests 42 and 43 km a day and gives 43

questions.q: A city has 1,25,00,000 people. Can all of them travel together in 4,000 trains that carry 1,200 people each? Show your working.
questions.a: No. 4,000 x 1,200 = 48,00,000 people can travel, which is less than 1,25,00,000. About 77,00,000 people would be left behind.
s: Concludes they cannot all travel and finds the 77,00,000 shortfall

questions.q: A bakery makes 1,200 rotis an hour. (a) How many does it make in a 10-hour day, and in 30 such days? (b) Assuming 30 days a month, can it make more than 10 lakh rotis in 3 months?
questions.a: (a) 12,000 in a day; 12,000 x 30 = 3,60,000 in 30 days. (b) In 90 days it makes 12,000 x 90 = 10,80,000, which is more than 10 lakh, so yes.
s: Part (a): 12,000 a day and 3,60,000 in 30 days
Part (b): 10,80,000 in 90 days and compares with 10 lakh

questions.a: Sample: 'A tea stall in Kolkata sells 150 cups a day. If it keeps selling at this rate for 20 years, how many cups does it sell?' Assumption: 150 cups every day, 365 days a year, no holidays. In a year: 150 x 365 = 54,750 cups; in 20 years: 54,750 x 20 = 10,95,000 cups, which is more than 10 lakh cups.
s: States a situation with a quantity per day (150) and a time in years (20)
States the assumptions (every day, 365 days a year) that make the stages valid
Interprets 10,95,000 as the total in the right unit and compares it with 10 lakh

questions.q: A printer prints 120 pages a minute. (a) How many pages in an hour? (b) How many in an 8-hour day, and is that more than 50,000?
questions.a: (a) 120 x 60 = 7,200 pages. (b) 7,200 x 8 = 57,600 pages, which is more than 50,000.

questions.q: Rohan says that since 250 babies are born every minute, 5 lakh babies are born in one day. Is he right? Work it out in stages.
questions.a: No. In an hour 250 x 60 = 15,000 babies; in a day (24 hours) 15,000 x 24 = 3,60,000, which is less than 5 lakh.
s: Compares with 5 lakh and says Rohan is wrong

questions.q: Show that you cannot count 1 crore coins in a 30-day month if you count one coin every second for 8 hours a day.
questions.a: Seconds in 8 hours = 8 x 3,600 = 28,800, so 28,800 coins a day. In 30 days: 28,800 x 30 = 8,64,000 coins, which is much less than 1 crore (1,00,00,000).
s: Compares with 1,00,00,000 and concludes it cannot be done

questions.q: A seed bank in Tumakuru wants to catalogue 1,00,000 rice varieties. Its cataloguing team, working every day, records 3 varieties a day together, and the bank plans to keep this programme running for 80 years. (a) How many days are there in 80 years (take 365 days a year), and how much less than one lakh is that? (b) How many varieties does the team catalogue in 80 years? (c) How many varieties a day, a whole number, would be enough, and how many above one lakh would that give? (d) The director says the team can finish the whole lakh at 3 a day within 80 years. Do you agree? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 365 x 80 = 29,200 days, which is 1,00,000 - 29,200 = 70,800 less than one lakh, so even one variety a day cannot reach a lakh. (b) 3 x 29,200 = 87,600 varieties. (c) 4 a day gives 4 x 29,200 = 1,16,800, which is 16,800 more than one lakh. (d) No. 87,600 is 12,400 less than 1,00,000; the team would need 4 a day.
s: Part (a): 365 x 80 = 29,200 days and 70,800 below one lakh
Part (c): 4 a day gives 1,16,800, which is 16,800 above a lakh
Part (d): disagrees because 87,600 is 12,400 short of 1,00,000

questions.a: (a) 10,000 lakh = 100 crore = 1 arab = 1,00,00,00,000, which has 9 zeros. (b) 5 arab = 500 crore, which is larger than 400 crore by 100 crore. (c) 1,32,000 - 1,00,000 = 32,000 more. One more than 99,999 is 1,00,000 (one lakh), the smallest 6-digit number.
s: Part (a): converts 10,000 lakh to 100 crore = 1 arab with 9 zeros
Part (b): converts 5 arab to 500 crore and compares with 400 crore (100 crore more)

questions.q: Dev says 'one lakh is a large number, full stop.' Anita says 'one lakh is small, because 1,32,000 people sit in one stadium.' Who is right? Support your view with one example each for 'large' and 'small'.
questions.a: Neither is right on their own: whether a lakh is large or small depends on what it is compared with. It is large for days in a life: 100 years is only 36,500 days, so a lakh days is more than two lifetimes. It is small for a city's people: a crore is 100 lakh, so a lakh is a hundredth of one crore people.
s: States that it depends on what is compared
Gives a 'large' example with numbers (36,500 days in 100 years against 1,00,000)
Gives a 'small' example with numbers (1 lakh against 1 crore = 100 lakh)

questions.q: Sonal says: 'A lakh has 5 zeros and a crore has 7 zeros, so a crore is 100 times a lakh.' Is her reasoning correct?
questions.a: Yes. Two extra zeros multiply a number by 10 twice, that is by 100. Also 1,00,00,000 / 1,00,000 = 100, and the book says a crore is a hundred times a lakh.

questions.q: Pune had 31,15,431 people in 2011. (a) Write this as lakh and thousand. (b) How much more is needed to reach one crore? (c) How many stadiums of one lakh seats each are needed to seat everyone?
questions.a: (a) 31 lakh 15 thousand 431. (b) 1,00,00,000 - 31,15,431 = 68,84,569. (c) 31 stadiums seat 31,00,000 and 15,431 people are left, so 32 stadiums are needed.

questions.q: At noon the counter at a Nagpur railway station shows 99,640 passengers for the day. On average 40 more passengers pass through every minute. (a) How many more passengers are needed to reach one lakh? (b) In how many minutes will the counter reach one lakh? (c) What will the counter show 15 minutes after noon? Write it with Indian commas. (d) A board says 'More than a lakh passengers by 12:15 pm'. Is that correct? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 1,00,000 - 99,640 = 360. (b) 360 / 40 = 9 minutes. (c) 99,640 + 15 x 40 = 99,640 + 600 = 1,00,240. (d) Yes. The counter crosses one lakh at 12:09 and shows 1,00,240 at 12:15, which is more than a lakh.
s: Part (d): says yes because 1,00,240 is above 1,00,000 (crossed at 12:09)

questions.q: At a school quiz, a calculator has only the buttons +10,000 and +100. A team earns a bonus if it shows 6,43,500 in fewer than 100 clicks. (a) Write an expression for 6,43,500 using the two buttons and count the clicks. (b) Can this calculator show 6,43,550? Explain. (c) Write a different expression for 6,43,500 that uses 63 presses of +10,000 and count its clicks. (d) Which expression earns the bonus, and why can no way use fewer clicks than yours?
questions.a: (a) (64 x 10,000) + (35 x 100) = 6,43,500, 99 clicks. (b) No. Both buttons add multiples of 100 and 6,43,550 ends in 50. (c) (63 x 10,000) + (135 x 100) = 6,43,500, with 63 + 135 = 198 clicks. (d) The first (99 clicks, fewer than 100). Each time one fewer +10,000 is pressed, 100 more +100 presses are needed, so the clicks rise.
s: Part (b): says no because only multiples of 100 can be shown
Part (d): picks the 99-click expression and explains fewer 10,000 presses cost 100 more presses each

questions.q: Use each of the digits 0 to 9 exactly once to make a 10-digit number (the first digit cannot be 0). (a) Write the largest multiple of 5 and say how you decided. (b) Write the smallest even number and say how you decided. (c) Write the smallest multiple of 5. Does it end in 0 or in 5? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 9876543210: digits in decreasing order, and it ends in 0 so it is a multiple of 5. (b) 1023456798: the first digit is 1 (not 0), then 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 in increasing order, and the last digit is 8, an even digit; this is smaller than the smallest ending in 0, which is 1234567890. (c) 1023467895, ending in 5. Ending in 5 lets the 0 sit in the second place, giving 10... which is smaller than 1234567890, the smallest number ending in 0.
s: Part (a): gives 9876543210 and explains largest digits first with last digit 0
Part (b): explains first digit 1, small digits early, last digit even
Part (c): says it ends in 5 and compares with 1234567890

questions.q: Tara says that when each digit 0 to 9 is used once, the largest multiple of 5 must end in 5 because 5 is bigger than 0. Check her claim.
questions.a: Wrong. Ending in 5 gives at most 9876432105. Ending in 0 gives 9876543210, which is larger because its first five digits 98765 are larger than 98764. So the largest multiple of 5 ends in 0.
s: Builds the best number ending in 5: 9876432105
Compares with 9876543210 and says the larger one ends in 0

questions.q: Pooja says: 'Every number that a calculator with only +100 can show can also be shown by a calculator with only +10, and the other way round too.' Is she right?
questions.a: Only the first half is right. Every multiple of 100 is a multiple of 10, so +10 can show it. But the other way round fails: 370 needs 37 presses of +10, while +100 can show only multiples of 100, and 370 is not one.
s: Says the statement is only partly right
Explains every multiple of 100 is a multiple of 10

questions.q: The expression (63 x 10,000) + (7 x 1,000) = 6,37,000 uses two buttons. Create another number which the same two buttons can show in exactly 20 clicks and write its expression.
questions.a: For example (12 x 10,000) + (8 x 1,000) = 1,28,000, which uses 12 + 8 = 20 clicks. Any a and b with a + b = 20 work.
s: Chooses numbers of presses a and b with a + b = 20

questions.q: Take the digits 7 3 5 1 9 2 6 4 8 in this order. (a) Strike out 4 digits (keep the order of the rest) so the remaining 5-digit number is as large as possible. (b) Strike out 4 digits so it is as small as possible. (c) Explain how you chose which digits to strike out for (a).
questions.a: (a) 92648: strike out 7, 3, 5, 1. (b) 12648: strike out 7, 3, 5, 9. (c) A large leading digit matters most, so the 9 must be the first digit kept; every digit before it has to go, and after it the digits 2, 6, 4, 8 are kept as they are.
s: Part (c): says the first digit must be the largest available and removes everything before it

questions.q: A sign painter in Madurai makes number plates from sticks. The digits need these sticks: 0 needs 6, 1 needs 2, 2 needs 5, 3 needs 5, 4 needs 4, 5 needs 5, 6 needs 6, 7 needs 3, 8 needs 7, 9 needs 6. He has exactly 30 sticks. (a) How many sticks does the plate 63,890 need? (b) How many does 88,078 need, and which plate shows the bigger number? (c) By how much is the bigger one larger? (d) A customer wants the largest 5-digit plate the painter can make with 30 sticks. Which should he make?
questions.a: (a) 6 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 6 = 30. (b) 7 + 7 + 6 + 3 + 7 = 30; 88,078 is bigger. (c) 88,078 - 63,890 = 24,188. (d) 99,999 needs 5 x 6 = 30 sticks and is the largest 5-digit number, so he should make 99,999.
s: Part (d): chooses 99,999 because it uses exactly 30 sticks and is the largest 5-digit number
